citations.narrative:
This was a search inspection.
The facility has continued to sell wild mammals into regulated activity without an active USDA Animal Care license. The
facility was licensed with USDA APHIS Animal Care but failed to complete the Re-license process prior to their expiration
date (30-June-2023). Their license was then cancelled, and the licensee was instructed by text message and a mailed
letter stating they cannot conduct regulated activity without a license. The facility has also previously been cited for
conducting regulated activity without a license.
In 2025, the facility sold 2 striped skunks as pets and 7 groundhogs, 18 Virginia opossums, 4 raccoons and 2 striped
skunks were sold to a USDA licensed B dealer. In 2026, the facility sold at least one striped skunk for the purpose of
public exhibition. Additional wild mammals have been sold to non-USDA licensed individuals.
Conducting regulated activity without a USDA license does not comply with the Animal Welfare Act or ensure that APHIS
officials can assess the care of the animals. The facility must obtain a license from the USDA to continue conducting
regulated activity under the Animal Welfare Act. Continuing to conduct regulated activity without a license is a serious
violation of the Animal Welfare Act.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
